question.problem: Find the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=(6x-1)(3x+1).$
question.worked_solution:
From the equation $y=(6x-1)(3x+1),$ we find that the roots of the parabola are ${x}_{1}=\frac{1}{6}$ and ${x}_{2}=-\frac{1}{3}.$ 

To find the axis of symmetry, we take the average of the roots, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{1}{6}-\frac{1}{3})}{2} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{1}{6}-\frac{2}{6})}{2} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{1}{6})}{2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{12}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the axis of symmetry is $x=-\frac{1}{12}.$
